test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 14 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
A shopkeeper declares the given three schemes of discounts. Which of the following schemes is most beneficial to a customer?

A. Buy 5 items and get 23 of the same items free

B. Two successive discounts of 14% and 37%

C. Two successive equal discounts of 39%
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount % for Scheme A = [Free Items ÷ (Paid + Free Items)] × 100 = (23 ÷ 28) × 100 ≈ 82.14%

Discount % for Scheme B = 14 + 37 − (14 × 37 ÷ 100) = 51 − 5.18 = 45.82%

Discount % for Scheme C = 39 + 39 − (39 × 39 ÷ 100) = 78 − 15.21 = 62.79%

Scheme A gives the highest discount, making it the most beneficial scheme for the customer.

**∴ The correct answer is Only A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Scheme A: Buy 5 items and get 23 free.

Scheme B: Successive discounts of 14% and 37%.

Scheme C: Two successive equal discounts of 39%.

**Formula Used:**

Discount % in Buy X Get Y Free = (Y ÷ (X + Y)) × 100

Successive discount of a% and b% = a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)

 Scheme A 82.14% Scheme B 45.82% Scheme C 62.79% 
• Effective Discount Comparison 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total items in Scheme A = 5 + 23 = 28

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme A = (23 ÷ 28) × 100

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme A = 82.14%

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme B = 14 + 37 − (14 × 37 ÷ 100)

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme B = 51 − 5.18 = 45.82%

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme C = 39 + 39 − (39 × 39 ÷ 100)

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme C = 78 − 15.21 = 62.79%

⇒ Comparing the overall effective discounts: 82.14% > 62.79% > 45.82%

⇒ The maximum discount is provided in Scheme A.

**∴ The correct answer is Only A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the overall effective discount is determined using the direct formula: a + b − (a × b ÷ 100).

Buy X Get Y Free

In promotional schemes involving free products, the customer pays only for X items but takes home a total of (X + Y) items. The actual percentage discount equals (Y ÷ (X + Y)) × 100.

Customer vs Shopkeeper Perspective

A higher percentage discount minimizes the selling price, which makes it highly beneficial for a customer. On the other hand, a lower discount percentage yields more profit margin for the shopkeeper.
